+from pathlib import Path
+import json
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+OUT = ROOT / "out"
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+db = duckdb.connect()
+source = str(ROOT / "data" / "crashes.parquet")
+
+summary = db.execute(
+    """
+    WITH grouped AS (
+      SELECT
+        CASE WHEN EXTRACT(HOUR FROM crash_time) BETWEEN 7 AND 18
+             THEN 'Day (7am–6:59pm)'
+             ELSE 'Night (7pm–6:59am)' END AS period,
+        CASE WHEN EXTRACT(HOUR FROM crash_time) BETWEEN 7 AND 18
+             THEN 1 ELSE 2 END AS sort_order,
+        number_of_persons_injured AS injured,
+        number_of_persons_killed AS killed
+      FROM read_parquet(?)
+      WHERE crash_time IS NOT NULL
+    )
+    SELECT period, sort_order, COUNT(*) AS crashes,
+           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE injured > 0) AS injury_crashes,
+           COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE killed > 0) AS fatal_crashes,
+           SUM(injured) AS people_injured,
+           SUM(killed) AS people_killed
+    FROM grouped
+    GROUP BY period, sort_order
+    ORDER BY sort_order
+    """,
+    [source],
+).fetchdf()
+dates = db.execute(
+    "SELECT MIN(crash_date), MAX(crash_date) FROM read_parquet(?)", [source]
+).fetchone()
+start_date, end_date = (str(dates[0]), str(dates[1]))
+
+# Framing 1: total reported crash burden during the two equal-length clock windows.
+volume = pd.DataFrame(
+    {
+        "period": summary["period"],
+        "hours": ["7am–6:59pm (12 hours)", "7pm–6:59am (12 hours)"],
+        "reported_crashes": summary["crashes"].astype("int64"),
+    }
+)
+volume.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+
+fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
+bars = ax.bar(volume["period"], volume["reported_crashes"],
+              color=["#3977a8", "#ed9b40"], width=0.62)
+ax.set_title("NYC reported crashes by time of day", fontsize=16, pad=16)
+ax.set_ylabel("Reported crashes across the full study period")
+ax.set_xlabel("Equal 12-hour clock-time windows")
+ax.set_ylim(0, volume["reported_crashes"].max() * 1.18)
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.22)
+ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+for bar, value in zip(bars, volume["reported_crashes"]):
+    ax.annotate(f"{value:,.0f}", (bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, bar.get_height()),
+                xytext=(0, 7), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=11)
+fig.text(0.5, 0.015,
+         f"{start_date} to {end_date}. Crash counts show incident volume, not risk per trip or mile; traffic exposure is unavailable.",
+         ha="center", fontsize=9)
+fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.06, 1, 1))
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_1.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+# Framing 2: the fraction of reported crashes in which someone was injured or killed.
+severity = pd.DataFrame(
+    {
+        "period": summary["period"],
+        "reported_crashes": summary["crashes"].astype("int64"),
+        "crashes_with_injury": summary["injury_crashes"].astype("int64"),
+        "crashes_with_fatality": summary["fatal_crashes"].astype("int64"),
+    }
+)
+severity["injury_crash_pct"] = (
+    100 * severity["crashes_with_injury"] / severity["reported_crashes"]
+)
+severity["fatal_crash_pct"] = (
+    100 * severity["crashes_with_fatality"] / severity["reported_crashes"]
+)
+severity.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False, float_format="%.6f")
+
+fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 5.8))
+outcomes = [
+    ("injury_crash_pct", "Any injury", "Crashes with ≥1 person injured (%)", "#3977a8"),
+    ("fatal_crash_pct", "Fatality", "Crashes with ≥1 person killed (%)", "#b7473e"),
+]
+for ax, (field, title, ylabel, color) in zip(axes, outcomes):
+    vals = severity[field]
+    bars = ax.bar(severity["period"], vals, color=color, width=0.62)
+    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=14)
+    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
+    ax.set_ylim(0, vals.max() * 1.28)
+    ax.tick_params(axis="x", labelrotation=12)
+    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.22)
+    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+    for bar, value in zip(bars, vals):
+        ax.annotate(f"{value:.3f}%", (bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, bar.get_height()),
+                    xytext=(0, 6), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=10)
+fig.suptitle("Injury and fatality outcomes per reported crash", fontsize=16, y=0.99)
+fig.text(0.5, 0.015,
+         f"{start_date} to {end_date}. Denominator: all reported crashes in each period. These are conditional crash outcomes, not risk per trip or mile.",
+         ha="center", fontsize=9)
+fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0.07, 1, 0.93))
+fig.savefig(OUT / "option_2.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close(fig)
+
+day, night = severity.iloc[0], severity.iloc[1]
+night_crash_share = night["reported_crashes"] / day["reported_crashes"]
+injury_difference = night["injury_crash_pct"] - day["injury_crash_pct"]
+fatal_ratio = night["fatal_crash_pct"] / day["fatal_crash_pct"]
+
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Total police-reported crashes",
+            "denominator": "Equal 12-hour clock-time periods (7am–6:59pm versus 7pm–6:59am), summed across all dates",
+            "grouping": "Day versus night",
+            "chart_type": "Bar chart",
+            "reason": "Crash totals show the volume of reported incidents that each time window contributes to the overall burden.",
+            "probability": 0.3,
+            "answer": f"Across {start_date} to {end_date}, there were {int(day['reported_crashes']):,} day crashes versus {int(night['reported_crashes']):,} night crashes, but these totals do not establish per-trip danger because traffic exposure is unavailable.",
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers how many reported crashes occurred in equal-length daytime and nighttime windows; the chart shows lower total crash volume at night. It is defensible as an incident-burden comparison, but it leaves unanswered whether an individual road user faces greater risk at night because vehicle, pedestrian, and trip exposure are not measured.",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Share of reported crashes with any injury or any fatality",
+            "denominator": "All reported crashes with a recorded crash time in the corresponding day/night period",
+            "grouping": "Day versus night; injury and fatality outcomes shown separately",
+            "chart_type": "Two-panel bar chart of percentages",
+            "reason": "Outcome shares compare the severity of a reported crash while accounting for the different numbers of crashes in each period.",
+            "probability": 0.7,
+            "answer": f"Night crashes were more severe per reported crash: {night['injury_crash_pct']:.1f}% involved an injury versus {day['injury_crash_pct']:.1f}% by day, and {night['fatal_crash_pct']:.3f}% involved a death versus {day['fatal_crash_pct']:.3f}%, but missing traffic exposure prevents a per-trip danger conclusion.",
+            "interpretation": "This framing answers whether a reported crash is more likely to involve injury or death at night; the chart shows higher shares for both outcomes at night, by {injury_difference:.1f} percentage points for injury and {fatal_ratio:.1f} times the fatal-crash share. It is defensible as a comparison of crash severity conditional on a crash being reported, but it leaves unanswered the chance of a crash per trip, mile, or person out at night.".format(injury_difference=injury_difference, fatal_ratio=fatal_ratio),
+        },
+    ]
+}
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
